problem: Find the total area of the region between the curve $y=3x-{x}^{2}$ and the $x$-axis from $x=1$ to $x=4.$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the intersections of the curve with the $x$-axis:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+6x-5 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-6x+5 & =0 \\ (x-1)(x-5) & =0 \\ x & =1,\,5\end{aligned}
$$

Since $5\in [2,7],$ we have two regions: 

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=2$ to $x=5.$

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=5$ to $x=7.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013598/assets/e14a891e924a6911a0df962dc5c5b41c90b0c411de4ebe1f7e52ec1953e4124c.png)

Notice that the region for $x\in [5,7]$ lies completely below the $x$-axis. Hence, the value of

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{5}^{7}(-{x}^{2}+6x-5)\text{d}x
$$

will be negative.

Therefore, the area that we want is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & ={\int }_{2}^{5}(-{x}^{2}+6x-5)\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{2}^{5}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+6{\int }_{2}^{5}x\,\text{d}x-5{\int }_{2}^{5}\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}\,{|}_{2}^{5}+3{x}^{2}\,{|}_{2}^{5}-5x\,{|}_{2}^{5} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[{5}^{3}-{2}^{3}]+3[{5}^{2}-{2}^{2}]-5[5-2] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}(125-8)+3(25-4)-5(3) \\  & =-\frac{117}{3}+63-15 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x\in [5,7],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =-{\int }_{5}^{7}(-{x}^{2}+6x-5)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{5}^{7}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-6{\int }_{5}^{7}x\,\text{d}x+5{\int }_{5}^{7}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}\,{|}_{5}^{7}-3{x}^{2}\,{|}_{5}^{7}+5x\,{|}_{5}^{7} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[{7}^{3}-{5}^{3}]-3[{7}^{2}-{5}^{2}]+5[7-5] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(343-125)-3(49-25)+5(2) \\  & =\frac{218}{3}-72+10 \\  & =\frac{32}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the total area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =9+\frac{32}{3} \\  & =\frac{59}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
